subject: Urgent: BrightCart escalation — latency spikes vs client-side retries
messages:
From: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightcart.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@brightcart.com>, BrightCart EngOps <engops@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: P95/P99 spikes — BrightCart storefronts degraded this morning

Markus / Monica,

We hit a severe regression in tail latency on the Redwood hosted API this morning between 08:40–09:10 PST. Our checkout service saw p95 jump to ~1.2s and p99 to ~3.6s, causing retries at the client layer and double-charges on a small percentage of transactions. The Datadog alert and traces are attached.

Quick summary:
- Window: 08:40–09:10 PST
- Impact: increased client retries, elevated 500/5xx observed by our gateway
- Business impact: several customer reports; we've paused a subset of traffic to mitigate.

Please confirm if this is on your side (hosted API) or if something changed in the SDK behavior. We need an RCA and immediate mitigation plan — our ops and legal teams are watching.

Attachments: brightcart_traces_1129.json, latency-heatmap.png

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Cho
Head of Platform Reliability — BrightCart

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightcart.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spikes — BrightCart storefronts degraded this morning

Tim — thanks for the flag and the traces. We're pulling logs now and looping in infra. Initial note: we see a small cluster of slow responses from the hosted API in the same timeframe, but also an uptick in retry attempts from your client IP ranges (per access logs).

Next steps from us:
- Immediate: We put a temporary routing rule to divert a small percentage of BrightCart traffic to a warm fallback pool to stabilize latency.
- Short term: Engineering will replay incoming requests from the window to replicate.
- Long term: we will produce a joint RCA.

Can you also attach the SDK config and retry settings you were running in production? That will help narrow blame.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightcart.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@brightcart.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spikes — BrightCart storefronts degraded this morning

Monica — attaching the SDK configs. We are using the Redwood Node SDK v1.8.2 with default retry policy except a lowered timeout at 800ms in the checkout path. We did not change config this week.

Attachments: sdk-configs.txt

We appreciate routing work but to be clear: our gateway shows host 502/504 and the user experience indicates service slowness even after retries. We need an answer quickly.

—Tim

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spikes — initial replay + traces attached

Team — replayed ~10k requests from BrightCart's window against our hosted cluster. Observations:
- About 0.7% of requests saw elevated server-side tokenization time followed by long tails in request processing; root cause appears tied to a mis-scheduled background compaction on a subset of nodes (internal ticket INF-982).
- Simultaneously, we observed a burst of client retries: ~2.1x above typical baseline, driven by short client timeouts (800ms). Those retries increased queueing and magnified tail latency for the affected nodes.

Attachments: replay_logs.zip

Recommendation: We should treat this as a combined incident — a transient server-side resource event amplified by client retry amplification. Immediate mitigations:
1) Keep rerouting BrightCart to the fallback pool for another 2 hours.
2) Offer BrightCart a transient rate limit bypass for critical checkout traffic.
3) Provide BrightCart a recommended SDK update: increase timeout to 2s and enable jittered exponential backoff.

I'll put together a draft RCA. Markus, do you want a customer-facing summary for Angela?

—Marissa
Senior SW Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightcart.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@brightcart.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spikes — initial replay + traces attached

Marissa/Monica — thanks for the analysis. BrightCart legal is still concerned about double-charges and SLA credits. Before we do SDK recommendations publicly, we need clear evidence showing how much of the impact was caused by hosted-side scheduling vs our client behavior. Can you quantify the amplification factor and point to timestamps where server CPU/compaction aligns with the retry bursts?

Angela (cc) — any additional logs on your side?

—Tim

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightcart.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Executive summary & next steps — BrightCart latency incident (Nov 29)

Tim / Angela — thank you for your patience. Below is a short executive summary and the next steps we will take jointly.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: A mis-scheduled background compaction on a small subset of hosted nodes caused elevated request processing times between 08:39–09:06 PST. This matches the window in your traces.
- Amplification: At the same time, BrightCart's checkout path had a lowered client timeout (800ms) and default retry policy; the resulting retry storm increased effective QPS to the already-impacted nodes, turning a ~0.8% server-side slow-request rate into a noticeable customer-facing outage. We estimate amplification increased error/slow responses by ~2x during the peak.
- Business impact: transient customer-facing errors and duplicate charges in a small percent of transactions. We're classifying this as a Sev2.

Immediate actions taken:
- Temporary traffic diversion to fallback pool (completed 11/29).
- Patch deployed to prevent compactions from coinciding with peak request windows (INF-982 closed).
- Shared recommended SDK config with BrightCart to increase client timeout to 2s and enable jittered backoff (see attached sdk-configs.txt).
- We will provide an itemized credit for impacted requests (proposal attached as HS-12345).

Follow-ups (next 7 days):
- Joint RCA doc with side-by-side timelines correlating server CPU/compaction markers and client retries (deliverable: 2026-12-03).
- Post-incident call with BrightCart engineers and customer ops (calendar invite to follow).

Attachments: joint-rca-draft.pdf (will be sent), proposal-credits.csv

If anything in the above summary looks wrong from BrightCart's telemetry, please call me direct and we'll adjust the timeline.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
